title: Equal Sum Grid Partition II
summary: Given an m x n matrix of positive integers, determine if a partition can be made by either a horizontal or vertical cut such that each resulting section is non-empty, has equal sums, or can achieve equal sums by excluding at most one cell, while maintaining connectivity within each section.
statement: Given an m x n matrix of positive integers, determine if a partition can be made by either a horizontal or vertical cut such that each resulting section is non-empty, has equal sums, or can achieve equal sums by excluding at most one cell, while maintaining connectivity within each section.
constraints: The positive grid contains between 2 and 100,000 cells.
Make one horizontal or vertical cut into two nonempty rectangles.
The sums must match directly or after discounting one cell while its remaining section stays connected.
hints: For a fixed cut, only the heavier side can lose a positive cell, and the removed value must equal the sum difference.
Sweep row cuts while maintaining value counts on both sides, then transpose and repeat for column cuts.
At each boundary compare sums; otherwise locate the difference in the heavy side and enforce endpoint removal for one-dimensional sections.
Counts establish whether the needed value exists, while rectangular connectivity is automatic after one removal except for an interior cell of a single row or column.
editorial: Counts establish whether the needed value exists, while rectangular connectivity is automatic after one removal except for an interior cell of a single row or column.

tests.explanation: A horizontal cut gives equal sums of five without a discount.
A vertical cut gives sums four and six; discounting the boundary value two preserves connectivity and balances them.
